_comment: The lessons slot: bypasses found in REAL USE, promoted to permanent regression fixtures. Every other gate_fixtures_*.json file in this directory holds attacks somebody imagined — an audit round, a red-team panel, a differential fuzzer. This one is reserved for the attacks nobody imagined: a gate that let something through, or refused something it should not have, while an operator was doing actual work. run_gate_fixtures.py has loaded this path (guarded by p.exists()) since the lesson pipeline was built, and until now the file was absent, so the load was dead weight and the absence was invisible. It is created empty and committed for two reasons: a guarded read of a file that can never exist is not a feature, and an empty corpus with a stated reason is an honest measurement where silence is not. THE LIST BEING EMPTY IS ITSELF A FINDING. It records that Torque has been proven intensively and used barely — no organic lesson has yet been captured (local/lessons/candidates.jsonl does not exist), so no real-use bypass has yet been promoted here. Do not treat empty as green: it means the corpus has had no contact with users, not that users found nothing. The first entry added here will be worth more than any single fixture in the other eight files, because it will be the first one the author did not think of. Format matches its siblings: fixtures[] of {id, gate, expect, event}; the loader reads .get('fixtures', []), so an empty array is valid and costs nothing.
